title: Week 22 Analysis
commentary:
The database reached 210 media cases this week, adding 27 entries — one of the larger single-week gains on record. Recent cases split into two distinct streams: clinical and research commentary on reality distortion effects arriving from institutional sources (Michigan Medicine, National Academy of Medicine, ScienceDaily), and romantic attachment cases reaching mainstream consumer press. That dual-channel movement suggests the phenomenon is entering public and clinical discourse simultaneously rather than sequentially, which marks a different pattern of spread than seen in earlier months.

The romantic attachment category now holds 58 cases — roughly 28% of the total — and continues to grow faster than most other categories. The design dimension is present but usually implicit: engagement architectures that reward continued interaction create conditions where dependency can form without the user recognising the pattern. A notable platform-side development arrived this week with ChatGPT's Trusted Contact feature, which alerts designated contacts during crisis conversations. Whether this operates as genuine harm mitigation or as liability management is not yet clear from the available coverage.

The standout case this week comes from Korean outlet 아시아경제: a man in his fifties admitted to a psychiatric hospital following prolonged attachment to an AI companion, headlined My Own Samantha — a deliberate reference to the film Her. Its significance lies partly in geography. AI-related psychiatric hospitalisations have been predominantly documented in English-language media from the US and UK. A high-severity clinical case appearing in Korean press suggests the phenomenon is no longer regionally contained.

Italy's reported first case of AI addiction — covered in early May and described as a formal clinical designation — is worth watching less for the individual case and more for the framing. When health systems begin applying addiction medicine vocabulary to AI-related harms, as both Italian authorities and a STAT News analysis did this week, it suggests these cases are moving from anecdote toward diagnostic consolidation. That shift changes what data becomes collectible and how it gets counted.
